subject: GreenLabs reserved sizing: phased bands + GPU-price trigger discussion
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@greenlabs.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity structure: need phased bands + price-trigger proposal

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re working through our infra budget for H2 and want to explore a reserved capacity plan tied to a deal — specifically: a phased commit (baseline + burst), clarity on how overages are priced, and a mechanism to protect both parties if underlying GPU prices move materially.

Can you put together a short proposal that covers: 12 & 24 month terms, a suggested baseline vs burst split for a company our size (~120M tokens/month), and an example clause that handles GPU-market shocks (indexation or trigger + cap/floor)? Also attach any RFP we submitted — I included it for reference.

Attached: GreenLabs_RFP_SAAS_31MAR2026.pdf

Appreciate a ballpark by end of day if possible — we’re on a tight procurement timeline.

Best,
Jordan
Head of Platform Ops
GreenLabs AI
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@greenlabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity structure: need phased bands + price-trigger proposal

Jordan — thanks, got the RFP. We can absolutely do that. High-level proposal below; attaching a quick schedule too.

Summary (high level):
- Term options: 12m and 24m (we recommend 24m for better unit economics with a phased ramp).
- Phased banding: Baseline (75% of expected steady-state), Burst pool (25% committed but metered for burst use), On-demand overage (billed at higher per-unit).
- Price-trigger: GPU Market Index trigger (30-day window) — if index moves >12% up for 30d, unit price re-sets per pre-agreed formula; downward moves produce partial pass-through credit with a floor. Cap on negative exposure to Redwood.

Why phased banding: reduces customer up-front spend, lets us provision predictable baseline capacity while retaining operational headroom for bursts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment on discount thresholds and approval path (looping Ben + Marcus).
2) Operational feasibility check on ramp schedule and canary provisioning (looping Karthik).
3) Send the short term-sheet for review (DocuSign-ready).

I attached an initial schedule (proposed_reserved_schedule.xlsx) with a baseline/burst split tailored to your token estimate. I’ll follow up with two price scenarios for 12m/24m before EOD.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Lead, North America

Soojin — good start. A couple asks from GTM/Finance before we present to customer:
- Please translate baseline/burst into GPU-hours and reserved vGPU equivalents (so finance can map to unit cost).
- Attach pricing worksheet (I prepared a template) — see proposed_reserved_schedule.xlsx.
- We should set internal escalation if customer asks for >28% discount off list for 24m — that needs EM/RevOps approval.

Jordan: FYI, we’ll include discrete scenarios (conservative / balanced / aggressive) and call out the approval steps for deeper discounts.

Ben Carter

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity structure: need phased bands + price-trigger proposal

Team — added three concrete pricing scenarios (see attached CSV). Quick summary:
- Scenario A (Conservative, 12m): minimal discount, higher unit price, no indexation exposure.
- Scenario B (Balanced, 24m): ~22% discount off hosted list, phased ramp (50/75/100% over 90d), indexation trigger at +/-12% with cap/floor, limited credit-back on downward moves.
- Scenario C (Aggressive, 36m): deeper discount up to ~32% with committed floor and explicit GPU-price pass-through clause; needs Exec sign-off.

Assumptions (GPU pricing sensitivity):
- Base GPU cost index (spot equivalent) = $0.80/token-hour (internal index).
- 12% move changes unit margin materially — we model P50/P90 outcomes.
- Tail risk: >25% GPU price jump in a short window is possible; that should map to an automatic right to reprice or a scheduled reconciliation.

Related HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/GL-2026-142 (for numbers & forecast).

Attachments: pricing_scenarios_v3.csv

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity structure: need phased bands + price-trigger proposal

Quick operational notes:
- Phased provisioning looks fine — recommend an initial canary at 50% for 30 days, then automatic ramp steps (50 -> 75 -> 100) triggered by utilization thresholds to avoid cold starts.
- Burst pool should be implemented as a dedicated burst queue with higher priced tokens and pre-warmed kernels; that minimizes latency spikes and KV cache churn.
- For the indexation clause, we need a fixed measurement source (we should reference a mutually-agreed GPU price index, e.g., \"GI-Redwood Composite\" with public feed link). Also include a reconciliation window and an operational fallback: route excess requests to hosted non-reserved capacity during emergency decommit with defined SLA and pricing.

Operational risk: scheduling ramp too quickly could cause local KV-cache misses for their largest models; recommend we include a 14-day soft ramp between steps for large-seq jobs.

Karthik
VP, Serving & Infra
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@greenlabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity structure: need phased bands + price-trigger proposal

Jordan — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise term sheet capturing the balanced path we recommend. High-level summary for GreenLabs:

Proposed path (recommended): 24-month phased reserve (Balanced Scenario B)
- Baseline: 75% of expected steady-state (reserved, provisioned immediately).
- Burst pool: 25% committed but metered for bursts (pre-warmed).
- Ramp: 50% baseline on day 1, 75% at day 30, 100% at day 90 (with 14-day soft ramp for very large sequence workloads).
- Pricing: 22% discount off hosted list for the 24m term.
- Price-trigger: GI-Redwood Composite index as measurement; if index rises >12% sustained for 30-day window, unit price re-adjusts per formula (cap + floor applied). If index drops >12% for 30 days, customer receives a partial credit (floor applies).
- Escalation/Approval: discounts >28% require EM/RevOps approval; aggressive structures (Scenario C) require Exec sign-off.

Attachments: GreenLabs_Reserved_Term_TermSheet_v1.pdf (term sheet), proposed_reserved_schedule.xlsx, pricing_scenarios_v3.csv

Next steps:
1) Jordan, please confirm if Balanced (24m) aligns with your procurement runway.
2) If yes, we’ll route the term sheet to Legal for small redlines, get Finance sign-off, and prepare DocuSign. Link provided: https://www.docusign.com/terms/GL-2026-142-term-sheet
3) Schedule kickoff: proposed 2026-06-15 for capacity planning call and onboarding timeline.

If you want, Ben and Marcus are happy to run a 20–30 minute deep-dive on the numbers with your procurement/infra teams.

Best,
— Soojin

Enterprise Lead, North America
